# Incident Report — Malware Infection, DESKTOP-RNVO9AT

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** (Intel NIC vendor prefix) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** (confirmed via DHCP option 12, NBNS Workstation/Server registrations, and mDNS/LLMNR) |
| AD domain | BEPOSITIVE.COM (DC: WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19 / 172.17.0.17) |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString exchanged between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17) |

Capture window: 2024-09-04 21:32:31 – 22:32:07 UTC (5,091 packets). The exercise's Suricata alert log timestamps (17:32 UTC) reflect a 4-hour offset (EDT), consistent with this window.

## 2. Malware Family

**Win32/Koi Stealer** — **signature-confirmed**.

The Suricata/ET ruleset fired `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits) directly on the `POST /foots.php` traffic from 172.17.0.99 to 79.124.78.197, corroborated by `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser` (50 hits) on the same stream. This is a named-signature match, not a behavioral/heuristic inference.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-control
| Indicator | Detail |
|---|---|
| **C2 endpoint** | `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP, no reverse-hostname resolved — malware connects to the hardcoded IP; no DNS query for this IP appears anywhere in the capture) |
| Check-in beacon | Repeated `POST /foots.php` to 79.124.78.197, first seen 21:35:07 UTC, then approximately every 60–90 seconds through the end of the capture (22:31:53 UTC) — 20+ beacons total, empty response bodies |
| Gate/config request | `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` at 21:35:11 UTC |
| Gate response | Plaintext token returned: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn\|qIOuKk7U\|http://79.124.78.197/index.php\|` (SHA256 of response body: `736f0cb5cc23435dad920dbe447efcf102e61c8691fa8528f5f39f386537f43e`, 61 bytes) |
| Data exchange | `POST /index.php` at 21:35:12 UTC — response body is RC4/XOR-style encrypted binary, 105 bytes (SHA256: `ed0855c1637e5f93be7d54acb2cb8872683a0e5eb670258abb1ebc41bfbf459`) |
| User-Agent (spoofed/stale) | `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)` — used on every malicious POST, the anomaly Suricata's "Fake Browser" rule keyed on |

### Malicious domains
None. No DNS resolution precedes the connection to 79.124.78.197 — the malware is hardcoded to the C2 IP, so there is no C2 domain to report from this traffic.

### Malicious URLs
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (beacon/check-in)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (POST — config/exfil channel)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (gate lookup)

### Transferred artifacts
No executable payload transfer is visible in this capture (no `.exe`/`.dll`/PE-header downloads observed in any HTTP object). The only content-bearing exchanges are the encrypted gate/config blobs listed above; their SHA256 hashes are given in the table.

### Secondary, unconfirmed indicator
A TLS session to **46.254.34.201:443** (SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) occurs in the same time window (21:35 UTC) as the initial C2 traffic, immediately before the `foots.php` beaconing starts, and no DNS query for this domain/IP appears in the capture (name was pre-resolved or cached). This connection is **not** matched by any Suricata signature and cannot be attributed to Koi Stealer from traffic alone — flagged here only as a suspicious coincidence worth follow-up (e.g. possible stager/dropper delivery site), not as a confirmed IOC.

### Noted but not corroborated as malicious
The alert log also shows internal SMBv1/NTLMSSP and Kerberos-principal-length signatures (`GPL NETBIOS SMB...`, `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow`) between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17. These are legacy/generic rules that commonly fire on ordinary Windows domain SMB and Kerberos negotiation; nothing in the traffic content indicates actual exploitation, and no lateral movement or additional internal victims were observed. Treat as informational, not confirmed compromise activity.

## Summary
DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as domain user **afletcher** on BEPOSITIVE.COM, is infected with **Win32/Koi Stealer**, confirmed by Suricata's ETPRO Koi Stealer CnC-checkin signature. The malware beacons to **79.124.78.197:80** via `POST /foots.php` roughly every 60–90 seconds and exchanges an encrypted configuration/exfiltration payload via `/index.php`, using a hardcoded C2 IP (no DNS lookups) and a spoofed IE7/Windows 10 User-Agent string.
